newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian T-bills open flat, eye on week's data.
newsitem.headline: Canadian T-bills open flat, eye on week's data.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened little changed on Monday, despite recent weakness in the Canadian dollar, with the market largely focused economic data being released during the course of the week, analysts said.

"They're basically unchanged actually, and it's really quite a good performance when you think that the currency has actually dropped a fair amount (Friday)," said Barry Davenport, senior vice-president of treasury with Bank of Montreal.
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill softened to yield 3.07 percent from 3.06 percent at Friday's close.

Among the key economic reports due out this week are the Canadian and U.S. consumer price index reports for April, out on Thursday. Investors will be scouring those and other reports for clues about the timing of the next likely move in U.S. interest rates, analysts said.

"It's quite a heavy week for economic data coming out for the U.S. and for Canada," said Davenport. He said markets are about evenly divided about whether the U.S. Federal Reserve will hike interest rates on May 20.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.43 percent from 3.44 percent from Friday.
The one-year T-bill firmed to yield 3.99 percent from 4.01 percent.
The call loan rate traded at 3.0 percent, in the center of the Bank of Canada's 2.75-3.25 percent target range.
